history.origins: Likely developed in the late 20th century as a simplified version of more complex betting games. It is part of a family of 'Social Penalty' games (Jeux Ã  boire) common in European university culture.
timeline: 1980s: Emerges in French student bars as a 'Filler' game.
1990s: Rules for the 'Double-Penalty' bluff are standardized.
2010s: Becomes a staple of 'Appero' culture (social pre-drinks) in France and Belgium.
Present: One of the most-played communal games for its simplicity and immediate social tension.
history.cultural: Associated with the phrase 'C'est pour qui?' (Who is this for?) as players decide which friend to target with a revealed card.
history.evolution: The transition from counting points to 'Drinking Penalties' (gorgÃ©es) made the physical stakes of the game more immediate and humorous for social groups.

setup.players: 4-6 is the 'Sweet spot' for memory tension.
setup.dealing: Each player receives 4 cards face-down. They have 10 seconds to mÃ©morise them and then cannot look at them again.

rules.objective: Avoid penalties by remembering your cards and successfully bluffing your opponents.
rules.gameplay: A pyramid of cards is built face-down (6-5-4-3-2-1). Each player receives cards face-down, looks once to memorise them, then may not look again. Cards are revealed from the pyramid one by one (bottom row left to right, then next row). When a card is revealed, any player may claim to hold the same face value and assign a penalty (drinks) to another player; that player may accept or call bluff. If bluff is called and the claimer had the card, the assigned player drinks double; if the claimer was bluffing, the claimer drinks double. Number of drinks often equals the pyramid row (e.g. row 3 = 3 drinks). Game ends when the pyramid is fully revealed.
keyRules: Memorise your hand once; no looking again.
Match revealed pyramid card by face value to assign penalty to an opponent.
Target may accept the penalty or call bluff; wrong call doubles the penalty.
Optional: summit (top) card may count for more; wrong card when called costs double.

strategy.basic: MÃ©morise by position! Instead of trying to remember '7, King, Ace, 4', remember 'Left 7, Middle-Left King, etc.'. Most players forget their cards within the first 3 minutes. If you are targeted, watch the other player's eyesâ€”if they hesitated for even a second before 'Giving' the penalty, they likely don't remember their hand and are just trying to get rid of a card. Accuse them immediately!
strategy.intermediate: The 'Sacrifice' Bluff: If you hold a 6, and a 9 is revealed in the pyramid, you can 'Give' the penalty pretending you have the 9. If the other player is a coward and accepts, you won! If they call your bluff, you take the penalty, but you've established a 'Dangerous' persona that might make them more hesitant to challenge your REAL cards later in the game.
strategy.advanced: Social Engineering (Targeting): Don't target the same person every time. Spread the penalties around based on who is winning (remembering the most). If you see someone has successfully proven their cards twice, they are 'Hot'. Never 'Deny' their claims. Target the players who have been 'Double-Penalized' alreadyâ€”they are likely flustered and more likely to accept a bluff.
tips: Concentrate! The summit card is worth 5 units, but a summit 'Denial' is 10. Don't risk the summit unless you are 100% sure.
If you forget one of your cards, treat that slot as your 'Bluff Slot'.
